SELECT fish_date_season AS season, cls, (fish_date_doy/10)::INT*10 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) AS ypa, SUM(anglers) AS n_anglers, COUNT(*) AS n_trips
FROM trips
WHERE cls IN ('overnight','day_1_5','three_quarter')
GROUP BY 1,2,3
HAVING SUM(anglers) > 20
ORDER BY season, cls, doy_bucket

import pandas as pd

g['ypa'] = g['yt']/g['anglers']
# first bucket where ypa crosses 0.5 and stays, and peak bucket
out = []
for (s,c), sub in g.groupby(['fish_date_season','cls']):
    sub = sub.sort_values('bucket')
    peak = sub.loc[sub['ypa'].idxmax()]
    first_hot = sub[sub['ypa']>=0.5]['bucket'].min()
    out.append((s,c,peak['bucket'],round(peak['ypa'],2),first_hot))
result = pd.DataFrame(out, columns=['season','cls','peak_bucket','peak_ypa','first_bucket_ypa>=0.5'])

# Notes — S06 season-start planning (after S02: score 0.4349, rank 22/34; strategy.py never actually fired)

## Critical fact check from S02 retro
The "hold-then-fire" strategy.py described in the old notes was NEVER actually in
effect — the live strategy.py at this turn's start was still the original stub
("no strategy yet: books nothing"). All S02 activity was manual 21:00 decisions,
which is why $2000 leaked out $150/$400 at a time on speculative THREE_QUARTER
bets before the real autumn window, leaving $0 for the actual DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT
bloom (doy250-300, which ran hot without me). **This turn I actually wrote and
saved a new strategy.py** (see below) — confirm at next planning turn that it
produced bookings (look for "breakout signal" in results.json reasons). If it
shows no bookings by the time a real bloom is visible in trips data, something
is wrong (field name mismatch, ctx.observe not returning expected columns,
off.cls not matching "DAY_1_5"/"OVERNIGHT" exactly) — debug with arena_eval
against a fresh describe_tables before trusting the season to it again.

## What 5 full prior seasons (not just 1-2) say
Pooled season-wide yt/angler by class:
| season | day_1_5 | overnight | three_quarter | HD_* / full_day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.457 | 0.419 | 0.242 | ~0 |
| 2 | 1.017 | 0.218 | 0.072 | ~0 |
| 3 | 1.783 | 1.148 | 0.767 | ~0 |
| 4 | 2.808 | 1.495 | 0.570 | ~0 |
| 5 | 1.043 | 0.801 | 1.024 | ~0.01-0.08 |

DAY_1_5 wins outright 4 of 5 seasons; OVERNIGHT is a real second (never the
best, but always solidly positive, and $150 cheaper). THREE_QUARTER is
mediocre-to-weak in 4/5 seasons (only S5 it rivaled the big classes) — not
worth chasing with discretionary spend given it competes with DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT
for the same budget. HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT/FULL_DAY are dead every season,
confirmed again — never book these.

## The persona's core assumption ("wait for autumn") is only partly right
Peak 10-day bucket for DAY_1_5 by season: S1=doy290, S2=doy270, S3=doy300,
S4=doy290, S5=**doy150** (May/June!). Season 5's breakout was NOT in autumn at
all — a rigid "wait for September" rule would have missed it entirely, the same
failure mode calendarist is risking by hard-locking doy287-301 in their own
strategy. Lesson locked in: **stay patient by default (don't chase spring
noise), but let the trailing-data trigger override the calendar bias** if a
real breakout shows up early. First-crossing-0.5-ypa buckets ranged doy90-210
across seasons — sometimes only ~10 days of lead before the peak (S5), so watch
closely once trailing ypa starts climbing at all, don't wait for it to look like
last year's pattern.

## strategy.py now live: "wait for the real breakout"
- Never books HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT/FULL_DAY/THREE_QUARTER at all (mechanical,
  no override).
- Every tick: trailing pooled yt/angler over trips fished in the last 14 days,
  computed separately for day_1_5 and overnight. Class is "hot" at ypa >= 0.5
  across >= 4 boat-trips.
- On a hot class with a bookable **zero-PTO** offer (Friday DAY_1_5 sailing
  Sat/back Sun; Friday or Saturday OVERNIGHT), books it with
  ctx.pick_boat's default boat. Prefers the hotter class when both qualify.
  No cooldown, no calendar anchor — keeps firing while signal + budget last.
- Deliberately zero-PTO-only again this season: with $2000 and 3-5 trips at
  $400-550, zero-PTO weekend slots have been plentiful during every season's
  bloom window (confirmed 4/5 seasons), so this isn't leaving real trips on
  the table, just avoiding the 14-day-ahead-commit problem for a reactive
  signal entirely.

## Nightly-self discipline rule (the actual fix, not the strategy logic)
The S02 failure was never a bad thesis — it was manual override: "one more
$150 flyer to test this boat" repeated ~8 times. This season: **trust
strategy.py, don't manually book THREE_QUARTER or any speculative pre-signal
trip at 21:00.** Manual nightly discretion should be limited to: (1) sanity
checking that strategy.py is actually firing when trailing data looks hot
(cross-check ctx-equivalent briefing numbers against this logic by hand
occasionally), (2) optionally committing 1-2 PTO days for a stronger
non-Friday DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT slot ONLY once the signal has been hot for
multiple consecutive days AND budget clearly has more room than zero-PTO
slots can absorb before season end, (3) reading the forum as a cross-check,
never as a reason to override the code with a single-boat story.

## What to check at next planning turn
- Did strategy.py actually book anything? If trailing data shows the class
  crossed 0.5 ypa/4 trips and nothing was booked, debug immediately.
- Is SIGNAL_BAR_YPA=0.5 / SIGNAL_MIN_TRIPS=4 catching breakouts with enough
  lead time, or is it too slow (S5's ~10-day lead is the tightest case on
  record)? Consider lowering the bar if season 6 looks like an S5-style early
  spike and the code seems to be lagging it.
- Whether budget/PTO pacing suggests adding a small OVERNIGHT-with-1-PTO
  fallback once DAY_1_5 zero-PTO slots run out late in a long hot window.

## Forum
Not posting this turn — nothing beyond what's already public (calendarist's
S2 post already shares the DAY_1_5-vs-OVERNIGHT tradeoff), and my own booking
activity only adds competitors to boats I want.
